About 25 years ago I had a closet full of Filson clothes and luggage that I'd bought over the years and used on countless backcountry fishing trips and other adventures. When I got rid of everything I owned about 12 years ago, I got amazing money for even the most worn out stuff selling it on ebay.  It tickles me to see Filson and these other brands become fashionable, not that I didn't always thnk they were great looking, but they don't generally have to put up with the wear and tear (at least generally) that they were made for.  It reminds me of a story a friend of mine told me about how thrilled he was when roads were washed out in Malibu, that he and all the others Range Rover owners, got to use the fire roads to get to to their offices in Santa Monica and  Beverly Hills.   Anyway, now I'm an old man living in Bali and find this all very amusing.

If you like the Jim Green boots but want a more narrow last, grab a pair of their shoellies. They developed the narrow last and it fits me way better and these shoes (or the baobab boots) look fantastic.

I’m sorry, but I will never understand the appeal of a short tin cloth jacket. The appeal of a tin cloth jacket is that it is strong, water resistant, and abrasion resistant. But a jacket that short means that in the rain you will get very wet. And a lined version? The lining is there to increase warmth, but the short length means that you will get far colder. Filson used to make longer coats that were actually a useful length. Now they seem to only make jackets which are the length of a jean jacket, which makes them completely pointless. Filson, if you are reading this, I’ve purchased two of your coats, but I won’t buy another until you start making them a reasonable length again.
